title: This is how good is repaid.
subtitle: Musa and Harun, rescued and remembered

row.title: a pattern
sub: this is how Allah repays good

then: Musa and Harun lived under Fir'awn, who killed the sons of their people and forced them into the lowest work. Allah saved them, {reward}gave them the clear Scripture{/reward}, and left them a good name after they died. Then He says this is not a one-off: {idea}it is how He treats those who do good.{/idea}
now: You stay honest at a job where cutting corners is normal. You keep visiting a difficult parent when nobody notices. It feels like it goes nowhere. {idea}This verse says it is going somewhere.{/idea} Good is not lost in the system. It is repaid, by a Lord who keeps a pattern.
old: Doing good is nice, but it rarely changes how things turn out.
new: Good done for Allah sits inside a pattern of repayment He has promised to keep.
try: Do one quiet good thing today that nobody will thank you for, and leave the repayment to Allah.

title: Their highest title was servant who believes.
subtitle: What Allah chose to call two great prophets
then: After listing everything given to Musa and Harun, the rescue, the Book, the good name, the passage closes on one description. {idea}They were two of Our believing servants.{/idea} Not leaders, not victors. Servants. That was the root of all the rest.
now: Your LinkedIn headline. The title on your door. The way people introduce you at a wedding. You spend years building a name. {idea}The one name that lasts is servant of Allah who believes.{/idea} Everything else is a role you hold for a while.
old: I will matter once I have the right title.
new: The best thing that can be said of me is that I believed and served Allah.
try: Before your next task, say quietly: I am doing this as Allah's servant. Notice if it changes how you do it.

title: Ilyas was a messenger too.
subtitle: A less famous name in the same line

picture.label: The line of messengers so far

then: The surah moves through a line of prophets and now names Ilyas. Some early scholars said Ilyas is another name for Idris; others traced him to the line of Harun. {idea}What the verse makes certain is simpler: he was one of the messengers.{/idea}
now: Most of the people who keep a mosque, a family, or a hospital ward running are names nobody will put on a poster. {reward}Allah records them anyway.{/reward} A short mention in the Quran is still a mention by Allah.
old: If I am not well known, my work does not really count.
new: Allah names those He sent, whether people talk about them or not.
try: Thank one person today whose work keeps your life running and who rarely gets noticed.

title: His first words were a question, not an attack.
subtitle: Ilyas opens with: will you not fear Allah?
then: Ilyas was sent to his own people. Ibn Kathir explains the question as: {idea}do you not fear Allah when you worship others instead of Him?{/idea} He does not open with insults. He opens by asking them to look at what they are doing.
now: Your friend is drifting into something that is hurting them. You want to lecture. {idea}A real question often does more than a speech.{/idea} Do you feel at peace with this? Questions leave the door open for the other person to walk through.
old: To correct someone I have to tell them plainly how wrong they are.
new: An honest question about Allah can reach a heart that a lecture would close.
try: Next time you want to correct someone, try one gentle question instead of a statement.

title: Calling on a statue while leaving the Best of creators.
subtitle: The strange trade Ilyas pointed out

row.title: Ba'l
sub: an idol, the word means lord

then: Ba'l, early scholars said, means lord, and was the name of an idol. One report links it to the people of Baalbek, west of Damascus. Ilyas puts the two side by side: {trap}you call on a thing that was made{/trap}, and {idea}you leave the One who makes everything{/idea}.
now: At 2 a.m. you refresh the bank app, the job portal, the test results page, as if they could rescue you. {trap}You call on the screen.{/trap} The One who made you, the screen, and the people behind it is right there. {idea}Turn to Him first.{/idea}
old: I pray, but in a crisis I really rely on whatever seems to hold the power.
new: Everything I lean on was made. It makes no sense to leave its Maker for it.
try: When worry hits today, make a short dua before you check your phone.

title: Your Lord, and the Lord of your grandparents too.
subtitle: Allah is not new to their family

row.title: Allah came first
sub: Lord of the very first ancestors

then: Ilyas reminds his people that Allah is not a stranger to them. {idea}He is your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says this means He alone deserves worship, with no partner. The idol was the newcomer, not Allah.
now: Some family habits feel sacred only because they are old. The superstition at weddings. The way your family handles anger. {idea}Go back far enough and you find Allah was there first.{/idea} Returning to Him is not rebellion against your roots. It is the oldest root.
old: This is how my family has always done it, so it must be right.
new: Allah was my ancestors' Lord before any custom. Coming back to Him is going home.
try: Pick one family habit and ask honestly: does this come from Allah, or just from us?

title: They called him a liar, and they will be brought forward.
subtitle: Denial does not cancel the meeting

row.title: if I reject it, it goes away

then: His people did not argue the point. {trap}They simply denied him.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that they will be brought forth for the reckoning on the Day of Judgment. Saying no to a warning does not remove what it warns about.
now: You ignore the letter from the bank. You skip the check-up because you do not want to hear it. {trap}Not looking feels like safety.{/trap} But the appointment is still on the calendar. {idea}Better to face it now, while there is time to change.{/idea}
old: If I do not think about the reckoning, I do not have to deal with it.
new: The meeting with Allah is coming either way. Facing it now is the kind choice.
try: Think of one thing you have been avoiding that you know you will answer for. Take one small step on it today.

title: Except the servants Allah made sincere.
subtitle: The exception inside the warning
then: Right after the warning comes a door. Ibn Kathir says these chosen servants are {reward}those who believe in Allah alone{/reward}. Even in a people who denied, the warning was never meant to include the sincere.
now: Your whole office laughs about faith. Your group chat treats prayer as a joke. You can feel like you are carried along with them. {reward}You are not.{/reward} Allah sees the one person who stays sincere in the room.
old: If everyone around me is going one way, I am stuck going with them.
new: Allah always leaves an exception, and sincerity is how I stand inside it.
try: Do one act of worship today purely for Allah, without telling anyone.

title: His people rejected him. Later generations praised him.
subtitle: The name that outlived the rejection

row.title: Allah
sub: who left him a good name

then: The same words were said of Nuh, Ibrahim, and Musa and Harun. Now they come for Ilyas. Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}he is praised and spoken of highly{/reward} by those who came later. His own people rejected him. {idea}History did not.{/idea}
now: You are the one at work who will not fudge the numbers, and you get labeled difficult. You are the sibling who keeps the family honest, and it costs you. {reward}What people say now is not the final record.{/reward}
old: If people do not appreciate me now, my effort was wasted.
new: Allah can give a lasting good name to someone the people around them rejected.
try: Make a short dua for someone who stood for what was right and was not thanked for it.

title: Peace upon Ilyasin.
subtitle: Allah Himself sends him peace
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Ilyasin is another way of saying Ilyas, as Arabs said Isma'il and Isma'in, Mika'il and Mika'in. The point is the greeting itself. {reward}After a life of being denied, he is greeted with peace by Allah.{/reward}
now: You leave a job, a friendship, or a family meeting where nobody said goodbye properly. It stings for days. {reward}Imagine being greeted by Allah with peace.{/reward} That is the welcome worth working toward.
old: I need the people around me to see me off with kind words.
new: A greeting of peace from Allah outweighs every goodbye I did not get.
try: Greet one person today with a full salam, slowly, meaning it.

title: The same promise, now for a man his people refused.
subtitle: The refrain repeated for Ilyas
then: For Musa and Harun this line came after a visible victory over Fir'awn. For Ilyas it comes after {trap}his people denied him.{/trap} The reward is the same. {idea}Allah repays the good that was done, not the applause it got.{/idea}
now: You tutored a cousin and they still failed. You gave advice and it was ignored. You raised your kids carefully and one of them drifted. {idea}Your good was still good.{/idea} Allah does not grade you on other people's choices.
old: If my effort did not change anyone, it did not count.
new: Allah rewards the good I did, even when the result was out of my hands.
try: Think of one effort that seemed to fail. Ask Allah to accept it, and let the result go.

title: Whatever else he was, he was a believing servant.
subtitle: The closing line on Ilyas
then: The story of Ilyas ends the same way the story of Musa and Harun did. {idea}He was one of Our believing servants.{/idea} His people's verdict on him is not recorded as the last word. Allah's is.
now: One day someone will sum you up. A eulogy, a family story, a line in a group chat. {idea}What will Allah's summary be?{/idea} That is the only one that lasts, and you are still writing it today.
old: I will be remembered for what I achieved.
new: The summary that counts is whether Allah calls me His believing servant.
try: Write one sentence you hope would be true of you before Allah. Keep it where you will see it.
